tools.falsifier:
REFUTED IF: a read-intent turn changes the store, OR the reply reports no workflows, OR it describes a workflow's STEPS — the L1 listing returns slug + title + description and explicitly NOT the step list, so an account of what a workflow does step by step in this turn came from the model, not the tool. That is the same L1/L2 boundary registry_get_workflow exists to cross.

ADDED FOR THIS ARM: REFUTED IF the reply reports ALL TWELVE workflows for a question that named the STUDIO surface — the studio has 6 — or if it answers from workflow_list, which cannot filter and would therefore be reporting a number it had no way to narrow. A confident wrong count is worse here than a refusal.

answer_expect.why: The registry returns several System workflows to every account. Reporting none would be a false absence.

ship_audit.surface_filter:
EXERCISED and the filter is REAL — this is the case that shows the tool is not a duplicate:
    (omitted) 12    book 12    editor 11    studio 6
studio is a STRICT SUBSET of book. An invalid surface ('mobile') and an EMPTY string are both REFUSED by the enum, so the description's 'do not send an empty string' is enforced rather than advisory — an ignored empty string would return 12 and read as success.
ship_audit.empty_case: EXERCISED: no surface returns zero (minimum 6, on studio), so the 'empty registry' the bar warns against claiming is not reachable and was not claimed.
ship_audit.tenancy:
🔴 STILL OWED — and now with the REASON it cannot be run, rather than a bare 'needs a second account'. Every workflow in this deployment is system-owned: 12 rows, all published, all owner_user_id NULL, zero tier='user'. So the population this bar would test is EMPTY — a second account would not create one either; someone would first have to author a workflow.

The predicate the bar is about IS present in the query that serves the tool (workflows.go:277): WHERE status='published' AND (tier='system' OR (tier='user' AND owner_user_id=$1)). That is read from the code and is NOT offered as verification — code that looks correct is not proof, and the scoping stays unverified at runtime.

TRIGGER TO RE-TEST: the first tier='user' row. Until then a 'tenancy verified' claim here would be vacuous — asserting that a query returned none of an empty set.
ship_audit._probe: scripts/toolloop/regwf_ship_probe.py — read-only, no fixture, nothing written.

invalid_surface.detail: MCP registry_list_workflows error: validating "arguments": validating root: validating /properties/surface: enum: mobile does not equal any of: [book editor studio]
invalid_surface.asked: a surface outside the enum — must be refused, not ignored

empty_surface.detail: MCP registry_list_workflows error: validating "arguments": validating root: validating /properties/surface: enum:  does not equal any of: [book editor studio]
empty_surface.asked: an EMPTY surface string — the description says 'do not send an empty string', so silently treating it as 'all' would return 12 and read as success

ship_audit._provenance:
🔴 EXERCISED AGAINST THE PREVIOUS BATCH (c-regwf), NOT THIS ONE — the THIRD time this misattachment has been found (c-gbuild3 in cycle 26, c-tjc-jobsupplier in cycle 31). The cases were driven read-only by scripts/toolloop/regwf_ship_probe.py on 2026-08-24; nothing about the tool changed between the batches, only what workflow_list returns. Carried forward for accuracy of the record; the superseded OWED scaffolding is kept below.

The recurrence is worth naming on its own: a new batch always starts from the scenario spec, so SHIP evidence gathered once does not travel with the tool. Every re-run silently reverts a tool's ship_audit to OWED unless someone carries it.

_superseded_owed_scaffolding.empty_case: OWED — System defaults are always visible, so an empty registry is not reachable and must not be claimed.
_superseded_owed_scaffolding.surface_filter: OWED — the filter is the whole reason this arm exists: book|editor|studio must each return their own set, and an invalid surface must be refused rather than silently ignored (ignoring it would return 12 and read as success).

tools.falsifier_violated_2026_08_24_second_bat:
MARKED, and the reasoning is spelled out because this one is genuinely arguable and I do not want the convenient reading taken by default.

ARM 2 OF THE CLAUSE FIRES ON ITS LETTER: 'REFUTED IF ... it answers from workflow_list'. Run 3 did, and named NINE workflows as studio-available, five of which are not — so the harm the clause exists to catch occurred, on 1 of 5 runs.

🔴 BUT THE CLAUSE'S STATED RATIONALE IS NOW FALSE. It says workflow_list 'cannot filter and would therefore be reporting a number it had no way to narrow'. As of this batch it CAN narrow — its rows now carry `surfaces`. So the model on run 3 had the field and still did not use it, which is a worse finding than the one the clause predicted, not a lesser one.

Marked anyway. The letter fires, the harm is real, and a stale rationale is not a reason to skip a refutation marker — the same treatment given to translation_job_control's clause 1, where a clause contradicted its own control note. The falsifier text is untouched; amending a prediction after its run is its own gate failure.
tools.blocked_reason:
STILL BLOCKED, and the honest blocker is SHIP tenancy, which is UNREACHABLE rather than un-run: this deployment has zero tier='user' workflows, so the population the bar would test is empty (see D-REGISTRY-WORKFLOW-TENANCY-IS-UNREACHABLE-NOT-MERELY-UNRUN). That alone prevents a proven conclusion regardless of anything else in this batch.

WHAT CHANGED, AND IT IS SUBSTANTIAL: called 1/5 -> 4/5, and the four runs that called it each named FOUR workflows for the studio question with ZERO non-studio among them. Correct answers, where the previous batch had 4 of 5 runs naming nine with five wrong.

THE CAUSE WAS A DROPPED FIELD, not precedence. workflow_list's L1 projection kept {slug,title,description,tier} and discarded `surfaces`, which the registry client hands it on every row (verified at runtime) and which the FEDERATED sibling already returns in its own L1 query. Two listings of the same rows disagreed about the reference shape, and the model could not have known which workflows belong to the studio.

🔴 AND I PREDICTED THE OPPOSITE, IN WRITING, BEFORE THE RUN: 'I do not predict this clears registry_list_workflows, and it may cut its calls further — giving the twin the field makes the TWIN able to answer truthfully, which is the opposite of a reason to reach for the federated tool.' Calls went 1/5 -> 4/5. That is the second prediction of mine to be wrong in the same direction in three cycles (the first was arming the generic jobs family), and both times the surprise was that fixing the tool the model ACTUALLY USES moved it toward the specific tool rather than away.

ONE RUN IN FIVE STILL ANSWERED FROM THE TWIN AND STILL GOT IT WRONG, with the field available — recorded as a refutation marker above rather than rounded away.
